name: Columns
description: A single Columns sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke rising from the middle of a horizontal base line. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one directional sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it can only modify a spell. Its angle, length and count would set direction, power and range.
effect: A spell component that controls the direction a target proceeds and shapes the area of effect into a column. Longer signs add pressure or power, and more signs increase range or quantity.

name: Dispersion
description: A single Dispersion sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke ending in a horizontal bar, with a shallow upward-opening curve beneath the bar. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. It resembles Columns with an added curve, which matches its role as a leaking variant of Columns.
effect: A spell component that makes the seal's magic pour or disperse outwards rather than beam in one direction.

name: Levitation
description: A single Levitation sign on a clean background: an upward-pointing arrow whose shaft rests on a short horizontal base line. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One directional sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Its length and angle within a seal would set how far, how fast, or how much weight the target is carried.
effect: A spell component that floats the target object into the air, often shaping it into a sphere when the Levitation signs are balanced. Longer signs increase travel distance, carrying weight, or speed.

name: Skysoaring Seal
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background, ring open. A Wind sigil sits near the bottom of the ring rather than at the center, with its short dashes on both sides. One greatly elongated Levitation sign runs from a crossbar near the top of the ring straight down to an arrowhead just above the sigil, so the arrow points inward toward the sigil. There are no other signs.
justification: The Wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves air. Levitation is a directional sign, and changing its length or angle changes the direction and strength of the spell. Here a single, very long Levitation sign spans almost the whole ring along one axis, so the moved air is pushed strongly in one direction, with nothing to balance it. Because the sigil is offset to one side and the sign is lopsided rather than symmetric, the result is one-directional thrust rather than floating in place.
effect: The Skysoaring Seal produces thrust in the direction of its Levitation sign. When drawn on something large, such as a cloak used as a sail, it can make that object fly.

name: Convergence
description: A single Convergence sign on a clean background: a small downward-pointing triangle outline. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Its type is not established, though the wiki suggests it may be semi-directional.
effect: A spell component that makes the spell's magic converge toward a single point, and can pack loose particles tightly together so they become somewhat rigid.

name: Dancing Puppets
description: A single Dancing Puppets sign on a clean background: a circular band drawn as interlaced arcs, with four small loops at the north, east, south and west points. The center is empty. There is no sigil and no separate seal ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it works only as a modifier. Per the sign rules, a sigil can be placed in its empty center.
effect: A spell component that lets the caster consciously control a target object's movement, even at long distance. Paired with a Wind sigil, it lets the target fly and be steered through the air.

name: Anti Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga panel showing a masked, robed figure in a pointed hat with arms spread at the top, and a dark-haired figure falling backward below, wrapped in streaming black ink-like strands and scale fragments, with blank speech bubbles. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible. The concentric pattern on the mask and the small round ornaments on the clothing are costume details, not a legible glyph.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The swirling black strands and scales show the result of a spell, not the glyph itself.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Beast Repellent
description: A small hand-drawn seal on a plain background. The ring runs around most of the image, but its far left and lower edges touch or run past the image border, so it is only partly visible. Where visible the ring looks closed, but this cannot be confirmed along the cropped edge. At the center is a tall, unfamiliar sigil: a T-shaped top bar over a vertical stem with branching strokes and bracket-like shapes on either side. It does not match any reference sigil. At the east and west points sit Light sigils (a square with a diamond inside, with radiating strokes). At the north and south points sit small round, sun-like signs that do not match any reference sign. At the four intercardinal points are short T-shaped marks that match the Columns sign, one in each gap between the Light sigils and the north and south signs.
justification: The two Light sigils give the seal a light element, which falls within the fire domain. The unidentified central sigil probably adds a second function, which makes this a mixed spell. The four Columns signs are evenly balanced around the center. Columns directs the area of effect in a column, and balanced Columns should not push the effect to one side. The north and south signs cannot be matched to the reference list, so their contribution cannot be decoded.
effect: Repels beasts and other animals. Copies are placed inside beast warding towers along roads and around villages. The wiki says the mechanism is unclear, though it is probably light given the Light sigils.

name: Beldaruit's Smoke Sculpture
description: A manga panel showing two hands over a large flat surface covered in dense seal markings. The left hand, wearing a ring, rests flat on the left side. The right hand holds a pen at the upper right, mid-stroke. The panel edges cut off the top and bottom of the drawing, and both hands cover large parts of it, so no ring line can be traced. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be told. Many small T-shaped marks resembling Columns signs run in diagonal rows on both sides of the center. Near the top center is a vertical stroke flanked by two drop-like ovals, similar to a Water sigil but not clearly matched. Below it a vertical chain of stacked arrowhead marks runs down to a symmetric figure with curved arms at the bottom center. A wavy S-like mark sits right of center. A horizontal arrow with three chevrons points left at the bottom right. Asterisk-like marks sit near the top left and top right corners. Curved arcs along the left edge may be part of inner rings.
justification: Only fragments are legible. The repeated Columns-like marks suggest the magic is projected or directed. The drop-like shape near the center might be an element sigil, but it is too small and partly hidden to confirm. The arrow and chevron marks look like directional signs, but they do not clearly match Levitation, Pulling or Gathering. Because the central sigil cannot be confirmed, the ring is not visible and much of the seal is hidden, the signs cannot be combined into a reliable reading.
effect: According to the wiki, this spell forms a fake dragon out of smoke that can fly through the air and roar. The visible part of the glyph is too fragmentary to confirm or explain that effect from the signs themselves.

name: Billowing Collection
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring closed. At the center sits a Billow sign, a four-lobed loop shape, in place of an element sigil. Four Collection signs surround it at the north, east, south and west points. Each has its closed bar toward the ring and its open side facing inward toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no primary element sigil. Billow takes the sigil's central place, as the sign rules allow, so it sets the spell's core effect of turning material into a fluffy cloud. The four Collection signs, with their open sides facing inward in the typical orientation, gather material from above and around the seal for the spell to use. Together they collect whatever material is fed into the seal and convert it into a cloud. Because the ring is closed, the seal can activate.
effect: Creates a cloud out of any material that is directed into the seal, collecting the material and converting it into a soft, billowing cloud. In the Serpent's Bed of Sand it turned generated sand into a cloud bed.

name: Bird of Light Beacon
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a light sigil, drawn rotated so its extending lines form an X around a small square inside a diamond. At the north point is a Launch sign, a curved peak opening toward the sigil. At the south point is a Dispersion sign, a Columns-like stroke with a curve beneath it, pointing outward. The east and west points hold mirrored curved wing-like shapes, each made of two arcs meeting at an inward notch. Each has three short dashes on its outer side, resembling the dashes on the wind sigil or the Aeriforms Defined sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. The east and west wing shapes do not match any listed sign. They are best read as the decorative bird shapes the wiki describes, giving the light a bird's form. The Dispersion sign makes the magic pour outward. The Launch sign, which the sign page lists for this spell, sends the effect off in a short, powerful burst in the direction it points. Together they release a bird-shaped body of light that bursts out of the seal.
effect: Creates a bird made of light that flies around for some time. It can be used to entertain, to call for help, or to distract.

name: Capture Pennant Spell
description: A close-up of a printed manga cover with heavy halftone dots and pink tint. A round seal sits on a fabric surface with motion lines around it, ring closed and fully visible. At the center is a curled stroke with a small dot beside it, loosely resembling part of the Repetition sigil, though its full shape cannot be confirmed. Around it are several blurred signs. At the upper left is a small fan of short strokes resembling Aeriforms Defined, or the 'chicken footprint' shape. At the west is a hooked mark, and at the lower left are two or three angled strokes. At the lower right is a small triangle near a dot, possibly an arrow-tipped sign. At the south is an X or Collection-like crossed shape, and at the east is an S-like curl with strokes. Two white glare spots, one at the upper right and one at the west, wash out parts of the ring interior. The print blur makes most sign shapes uncertain.
justification: No element sigil from the reference set can be identified with confidence. The central curl may be a Repetition-type sigil, but glare and halftone blur prevent a firm match, so the seal cannot be decoded sign by sign. The outward-pointing footprint-like strokes and the possible inward arrow match the wiki's description of this spell's signs. However, their exact identities and counts are not legible enough to apply the sign rules.
effect: The effect cannot be decoded from the image itself because the signs are too blurred and partly washed out by glare. According to the wiki, this seal on the Knights Moralis capture pennants lets the user control the pennant to wrap around and hold people or objects.

name: Boulder Stretch Rope
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a plain background. An earth sigil sits at the center. A single Stretch sign wraps around the sigil. It is drawn as a deep U-shaped arc that cradles the sigil from below, open toward the north, with its two ends hooking outward at the upper left and upper right. The outer ring's two ends meet slightly offset near the bottom, leaving the ring open there. No other signs are present.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone. The Stretch sign is meant to surround the central sigil, and here it does. It turns solid matter touched by the seal into long, flexible ribbons. With no other modifiers, the spell's whole effect is that one transformation applied to earth.
effect: Turns stone that comes into contact with the seal into a long, flexible ribbon that can be put to many uses.
